title: All-or-Nothing Claim Design Creates Griefing Vector
description: The claim() function reverts if ANY token is paused, blocking ALL claims entirely. This is inconsistent with calculateClaimAmount() which skips paused tokens. A single paused token can block the entire protocol's yield distribution.
impact: Single paused token blocks entire protocol yield distribution. This creates a griefing vector where pausing one problematic token (which may be necessary for security) inadvertently prevents all legitimate claims across all other tokens.
attackPath: Admin pauses one token due to detected issue
All claim() calls now revert regardless of which tokens user wants
calculateClaimAmount() returns valid amounts (skips paused tokens)
Users see available yield but cannot claim any of it
recommendation: Make claim() behavior consistent with calculateClaimAmount() by skipping paused tokens instead of reverting. Alternatively, allow users to specify which tokens they want to claim, excluding paused ones.
